title: Nationwide Consumer and Fuel Retailer Choice Act of 2025
official_title: To amend the Clean Air Act with respect to the ethanol waiver for Reid Vapor Pressure under that Act, and for other purposes.
likelihoodReason: The sponsor is a Republican in the Republican-majority House, the bill has 55 cosponsors, and it passed the House. The year-round E15 change has support tied to ethanol production, while the provisions cutting small refining companies' renewable-fuel obligations by 75 percent and barring reallocation of those volumes may draw opposition from biofuel producers, and Senate passage would require 60 votes.
summary: This bill lets gasoline blended with 10 to 15 percent ethanol (E15) be sold year-round by extending the Clean Air Act's vapor-pressure waiver to those blends. It also cuts renewable-fuel compliance obligations for small refining companies and changes how their exemption petitions are handled.
brief: Allows year-round sale of 10 to 15 percent ethanol gasoline and reduces small refining companies' renewable-fuel obligations by 75 percent.

top_lines.headline: Year-Round E15 Ethanol Blends
subs: Extends the Reid Vapor Pressure waiver to 10 to 15 percent ethanol blends
EPA must update E15 pump labels and storage-tank rules within 18 months

top_lines.headline: Small Refining Company Obligations
subs: Defines 'small refining company' as under 75,000 barrels per day in 2025
Cuts their renewable-fuel compliance requirements 75 percent from 2028
Bars reallocating those obligations to other refiners

top_lines.headline: Small Refinery Exemptions
subs: Ends exemption-extension petitions for years after 2027
New closure-risk exemption capped at 150 million gallons for 2028
Returns retired credits for 2016 to 2018 compliance years

items.main: Extends the Clean Air Act's Reid Vapor Pressure treatment from 10 percent to 10 to 15 percent ethanol blends, allowing E15 to be sold during the high-ozone summer season.
items.detail: Amends Sections 211(f)(4) and 211(h) of the Clean Air Act so that a fuel meeting the vapor-pressure conditions can be introduced into commerce. For any State whose Governor submitted a notification after January 1, 2022, the paragraph (4) vapor-pressure limit applies to gasoline blends containing 10 to 15 percent denatured anhydrous ethanol.

items.main: Requires the EPA to finalize a rule within 18 months modifying E15 fuel-dispenser labeling and underground storage-tank regulations.
items.detail: The rule, issued after notice and public comment, must address compatibility of gasoline-ethanol blends greater than 10 and up to 15 volume percent ethanol under the Clean Air Act and the Solid Waste Disposal Act.

items.main: Creates a 'small refining company' category for producers whose 2025 daily average obligated-fuel production did not exceed 75,000 barrels per day, including affiliated entities.
items.detail: The definition reaches groups of affiliated entities linked through subsidiaries, parent companies, joint ventures, holding companies, or spin-offs. Beginning in 2028, the Administrator must reduce each small refining company's compliance requirements by 75 percent, subject to losing eligibility if production later exceeds the limit.

items.main: Ends the small refinery exemption-extension petition process after compliance year 2027 and bars reallocating reduced obligations to other refiners.
items.detail: No small refinery may petition for an extension for any calendar year after 2027, no petition submitted after July 1, 2028 may be considered, and outstanding petitions must be acted on by October 1, 2028. For 2028 and later, the Administrator may not reallocate a small refining company's reduced renewable-fuel obligation to other persons.

sections.label: Section 1(d)-(g) - Small Refinery Credits and At-Risk Exemptions

items.main: Returns retired renewable-fuel credits to certain small refineries for the 2016 through 2018 compliance years.
items.detail: Eligible credits are returned and deemed eligible for future compliance years or applied in the refinery's EPA Moderated Transaction System account. Eligibility depends on having submitted petitions that remained outstanding as of December 1, 2022, among other conditions.

items.main: Creates a new exemption for at-risk qualifying small refineries facing imminent closure, capped at 150 million gallons of biofuel-equivalent volume for 2028.
items.detail: A qualifying small refinery may petition by December 31 if it is at imminent risk of closure, permanent idling, or conversion solely due to compliance costs; the Administrator must act within 90 days. Petitions are not treated as confidential business information and must be made public within 30 days.

underreported.section: Section 1(c) - Adjusted Compliance Requirements for Small Refining Companies
underreported.summary: Reduces the renewable-fuel compliance requirements of each small refining company by 75 percent beginning in 2028 and bars reallocating the reduced volumes to other refiners.
underreported.why_unreported: The bill's title concerns the ethanol vapor-pressure waiver, but this provision cuts renewable-fuel obligations for a class of refiners defined broadly to include affiliated corporate groups.

underreported.section: Section 1(g)(iii) - Public Disclosure of Exemption Petitions
underreported.summary: Bars at-risk small refinery exemption petitions from confidential-business-information treatment and requires public release within 30 days of submission.
underreported.why_unreported: This makes ordinarily confidential refinery compliance filings public, an effect not implied by a bill about the ethanol waiver.

criticisms.why: I rise to express my strong opposition to H.R. 1346. This bill is disastrous for Wyoming refiners and independent petroleum producers, leading to a direct loss of at least 750 jobs in my home State. Just to correct the record, it isn't the farmers who produce ethanol or E15. It is the refiners, and this bill threatens to put them out of business. In fact, it is interesting that anyone who supports this bill has not yet mentioned the fact that it is the refiners that will be forced, mandated, to meet the E15 requirement.

I appreciate my colleagues on both sides of this debate and where they are coming from. I understand my friends who come from States that want support for farming. We all want to make sure that we are figuring that out. We worked through the farm bill. I just think we ought to be going about this a different way. If we need to do something to support farmers, let's have a direct conversation about it. Expanding E15 is just the wrong direction to go. It is going to harm refiners. It is going to drive up the cost of gas.

gaps: The bill enables year-round sale of blends up to 15 percent ethanol but does not address blends above 15 percent ethanol.

The bill cuts small refining companies' compliance requirements by 75 percent and bars reallocation of those volumes but does not state how the resulting shortfall in obligated renewable fuel is absorbed.
The bill caps 2028 at-risk exemptions at 150 million gallons of biofuel-equivalent volume but does not specify how the Administrator prioritizes competing petitions if they exceed the cap.
The bill requires EPA to modify E15 labeling and storage-tank rules within 18 months but sets no date by which the modified rule must take effect.

featured_quotes.name: Ms. Hageman
featured_quotes.text: I rise to express my strong opposition to H.R. 1346. This bill is disastrous for Wyoming refiners and independent petroleum producers, leading to a direct loss of at least 750 jobs in my home State. Just to correct the record, it isn't the farmers who produce ethanol or E15. It is the refiners, and this bill threatens to put them out of business. In fact, it is interesting that anyone who supports this bill has not yet mentioned the fact that it is the refiners that will be forced, mandated, to meet the E15 requirement.

featured_quotes.name: Mr. Roy
featured_quotes.text: I appreciate my colleagues on both sides of this debate and where they are coming from. I understand my friends who come from States that want support for farming. We all want to make sure that we are figuring that out. We worked through the farm bill. I just think we ought to be going about this a different way. If we need to do something to support farmers, let's have a direct conversation about it. Expanding E15 is just the wrong direction to go. It is going to harm refiners. It is going to drive up the cost of gas.

featured_quotes.name: Ms. Budzinski
featured_quotes.text: As a lead Democrat on this bill, I have been proud to work with Congressman Adrian Smith on this issue. We both understand, like many other Members, that year-round E15 is bigger than politics. This is about American farmers. It is about American consumers, and it is about American energy. E15 is truly one of those rare issues where everyone wins. Here is why: American farmers win because it creates strong and stable markets for homegrown corn. American consumers win because E15 helps to lower prices at the pump.

featured_quotes.name: Mrs. Miller-Meeks
featured_quotes.text: Every single year since 2011, the EPA has issued an emergency waiver to allow E15 to be sold during the Speaker, I yield 2 minutes to the gentlewoman from Iowa (Mrs. Miller-Meeks), a valued member of the Energy and Commerce Committee.

featured_quotes.name: Mr. Finstad
featured_quotes.text: As a fourth-generation corn and soybean farmer from southern Minnesota raising that fifth generation and representing 21 counties in southern Minnesota, a very strong egg-producing district, I have had many conversations with my neighbor farmers. I know by hearing what they are telling me and firsthand in my own experience as a farmer that we are facing uncertainty in our input costs and uncertainty in the global markets. We need a new domestic opportunity for our corn. E15 delivers on that.

added: A 'small refining company' category for producers under 75,000 barrels per day in 2025
A closure-risk exemption for at-risk qualifying small refineries, capped at 150 million gallons of biofuel-equivalent volume for 2028
A requirement that EPA modify E15 dispenser labeling and underground storage-tank rules within 18 months
modified: The Reid Vapor Pressure ethanol threshold changed from 10 percent to 10 to 15 percent in Section 211(h) of the Clean Air Act
Small refining companies' renewable-fuel compliance requirements reduced by 75 percent beginning in 2028
removed: Small refinery exemption-extension petitions ended for calendar years after 2027, with no petitions considered after July 1, 2028
The Administrator barred from reallocating reduced small refining company obligations to other refiners for 2028 and later
